question.text: The financial markets enable efficient transfer and allocation of resources. Who acts as INTERMEDIARY between providers of surplus funds and users of funds per Ch 1.1.1?

answer.text: Only the Ministry of Finance directly disburses surplus funds
Banks, financial institutions, mutual funds and insurance companies channelize surplus funds from lenders to users
Only RBI and SEBI - the regulators themselves

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook p.33 (Ch 1.1.1) states that banks, financial institutions, mutual funds and insurance companies channelize surplus funds from lenders to users of funds. That sentence is the source-backed basis for the keyed answer. The Trap: Option A confuses policy disbursement with market intermediation. Option C narrows the channel to peer-to-peer platforms only. Option D conflates regulation with intermediation - RBI and SEBI supervise the system rather than act as intermediaries themselves. Note: The answer rests on the p.33 intermediary list; cite that page when explaining the choice.
